items.title: An anti-equivalence between systems of finite type algebras and finite type maps of affine formal algebraic spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space X over a scheme with associated weakly admissible topological ring A, the lemma establishes an anti-equivalence between the category of inverse systems of finite type algebras over the quotients of A, with compatible transition maps inducing isomorphisms modulo the earlier quotients, and the category of finite type maps of affine formal algebraic spaces into X (statement lines 6404-6415). The proof constructs both functors and then checks that they are quasi-inverse. From a map into X it takes the fibre products with the quotients of A, notes that they are affine and that the resulting ring maps are of finite type, so that the system of their coordinate rings is an object of the first category (proof lines 6417-6424). In the other direction it takes the colimit of the spectra of the members of a system, which is an affine formal algebraic space, and verifies that its fibre product with a quotient of A is the corresponding member of the system by evaluating on quasi-compact test objects: a morphism from such a test object into the fibre product factors through one of the stages by two applications of the factorization lemma, and the second axiom on the system identifies that stage (proof lines 6426-6445). The same evaluation then shows that the resulting map into X is of finite type, since any quasi-compact test object over X factors through a quotient of A (proof lines 6445-6458). Finally the two composites are seen to be the identity, once by the computation just made and once by evaluating on quasi-compact test objects and writing X as the colimit of its quotients (proof lines 6460-6478). The claim is H2: it is one coherent construction, but each of the three verifications -- that the colimit computes the expected fibre products, that the map obtained is of finite type, and that the composites are identities -- is carried out rather than assumed.
